verdicts.flaw_description: A second change hit every unit at the same time: 'Each shop moved its machines to a coated carbide insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines.' The new insert grade reaches all four runs (all switched 4-7 March), so the 4-7 minute savings are equally explained by the inserts rather than the coolant.

The measured runs are not the upgraded condition: 'The figures cover every scheduled run at each stack, and a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed.' The 8-14 percent reductions are aggregates over a population in which one run in four had the new filter out of line, so the figures do not measure particulate under the upgrade.

The post-adoption numbers cover a narrower population than the claim: 'Rates cover the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol, and a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol.' The 6-11 percent figures are computed on a self-selected 75 percent of patients (those with no off-protocol spells, plausibly the shorter, less complicated stays) and compared against the whole ward a quarter earlier, so they are not the ward infection rate the claim is about.

The 'after' figures are a selected subset: 'Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices, and about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices.' The 4-7 percent rise is measured on the 80 percent of orders that happened to ring at the new price and compared to the whole line a month earlier, so the gap may reflect which orders fell into that subset rather than the pricing rule.

The scored trays are not all the treated condition: 'Rates cover every tray sown from each lot, full coat or partial, and about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed.' The 6-11 point gains pool fully coated with partly coated trays, so the figures do not measure germination under the coating as the claim describes it.

Two of the four cohorts are measured before the app started: cohort One 'started 4 April; by 29 March resting heart rate ran 5 bpm below', and cohort Three 'started 5 October; by 30 September ... 6 bpm below'. Those drops predate enrolment and cannot have been caused by the app.
